newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close stable to lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close stable to lower.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed Monday stable to slightly lower in a cautious market ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve Federal Open Market Committee meeting Tuesday and Wednesday, dealers said.
"There was little volume, and little activity as the year-end comes nearer," said a broker at a huge foreign bank.
"There is no nervousness abouth the Fed, as most people don't expect rates to move. Most investors are not taking new positions ahead of the meeting, but just out of caution."
The FRB shed 3/8 to 85-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at $122.10.
Volume was moderate although some dealers mentioned heavy trade with FRBs.
"The market was very calm in spite of the Dow's decline," a dealer at another foreign bank said. The Dow Jones closed 0.58 percent lower at 6268.35.
"Argentine bonds moved all day within a narrow range but quite firm."
Dealers said new charges of corruption in the government launched Sunday by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo had virtually no impact on the market.
